## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (apa.org/pubs/journals/abn) and Wikipedia editorial history gathered 2026-05. **Note**: Journal renamed from *Journal of Abnormal Psychology* to *Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science* in 2022 (anti-stigma editorial decision). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — international clinical-science authorship; cross-cultural psychopathology mechanism research published |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium — non-Western data accepted; non-Western theoretical frameworks less common |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — anti-stigma editorial line; framing of mental illness as part of human diversity rather than deviation |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Clinical science mechanism research — child/adolescent (1,542 articles), mental health (1,091), anxiety/depression mechanisms (774), personality disorders (641), schizophrenia (556) per OpenAlex |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **mechanism-focused clinical-science contribution** — psychopathology process, treatment mechanism, or transdiagnostic mechanism research. Anti-stigma framing expected (mental illness as part of human diversity, per 2022 rename rationale).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Format-noncompliant manuscripts returned without review. Stigmatizing language (e.g., "abnormal," "disordered") may receive editorial comment.

| Mixed methods | 2 | Accepted with quantitative dominance |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed; PRISMA reporting expected |

| **Writing style notes** | APA 7th edition for revisions; clinical-science vocabulary; anti-stigma terminology preferred; mechanism-process language; ScholarOne Manuscripts platform |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the clinical-science + psychopathology mechanism research community — APA Division 12 (Society of Clinical Psychology) faculty plus clinical-neuroscience researchers. Strong reproducibility / open-science emphasis. Common reviewer demands: "Mechanism specificity?", "Transdiagnostic relevance?", "Open data and preregistration?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |

| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International clinical-science programs; APA Division 12 affiliations | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journal_of_Abnormal_Psychology |

### AI-Research Notes (supplementary AI research, 2026-07-13)

> Added as a **supplementary, independent research pass** — it does NOT overwrite or supersede the Tier assessment above. Treat conflicts as a signal to re-verify, not as an automatic correction. Overall `signal_quality` for this pass: **2/5**.

**AI-research finding (policy):** This is the APA-wide (all APA journals, not JPCS-specific) generative AI policy, linked from the JPCS submission-guidelines page. No permission gate: AI use is permitted but must be disclosed in the Methods (or most relevant) section with tool name and, where relevant, prompts cited; AI cannot be listed as an author; authors bear full responsibility for accuracy of AI-assisted content. No JPCS-specific AI statement was found beyond a link to this general policy, so this is publisher-policy-level signal only (not journal-specific first-hand evidence), hence signal_quality capped at 2.

**AI-research finding (positioning — what the journal accepts now):** Basic research/theory and methodology in psychopathology broadly: etiology, development, symptomatology and course of psychopathology; basic psychological processes in individuals with mental illness; maladaptive processes in nonclinical/community samples; descriptive and experimental studies of disordered thoughts/emotions/behavior; sociocultural effects on pathological processes; new or novel-application methodology for measuring psychopathology and its mechanisms.

**AI-research finding (experiential):** SciRev page explicitly marks acceptance rate, immediate-rejection rate, articles-published and manuscripts-received as 'n/a' (editor never supplied them). One SciRev respondent's outcome was logged simply as 'Rejected (im.)' with no further detail. SciRev respondents rated reviewer-comment difficulty 4.0/5 ('difficult') and review-report quality 4.0/5, with overall handling rated 4.0/5 — but this rests on only 3 SciRev reviews for a discontinued journal title, so treat as indicative at best, not representative.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Stigmatizing framing of mental illness (community evidence: 2022 rename rationale)
- Pure qualitative submissions
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy
- Manuscripts outside psychopathology / clinical-science scope
- Format-noncompliant submissions returned without review

### Soft Tax

Low for clinical-science mechanism authors aligned with open-science values. Moderate for pathologizing-framework authors — must adapt to anti-stigma editorial line. Format-free initial submission; APA 7th edition required on revision.

### Best Suited For

- Psychopathology mechanism research
- Transdiagnostic process studies
- Mental health treatment mechanism research
- Clinical-science empirical work with open-science / preregistration
- Schizophrenia, eating disorders, personality disorders mechanism research
- Meta-analyses of psychopathology mechanism literatures

### Not Recommended For

- Pure autoethnography or first-person mental-illness narratives
- Critical / discursive mental-health work (consider Theory & Psychology)
- Treatment outcome RCTs (consider JCCP)
- Manuscripts using stigmatizing terminology
- Authors needing rapid turnaround

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology](./journal-of-consulting-and-clinical-psychology.md) | If recast as treatment-outcome work; APA family |
| 2 | [Clinical Psychology Review](./clinical-psychology-review.md) | If recast as systematic review; Elsevier; clinical-review specialty |
| 3 | [Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry](./journal-of-child-psychology-and-psychiatry.md) | If child/adolescent focused; ACAMH / Wiley |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general clinical-psychology venue as "too mechanism-focused," J Psychopathology and Clinical Science is often a better fit because: it specializes in psychopathology mechanism research; strong open-science / preregistration culture; anti-stigma editorial line provides framing safety; and APA Division 12 affiliation provides built-in clinical audience.
